2 trapped Nepal workers rescued from tunnel 9 days after devastating floods

3 hours ago CBS News ,

Nepal flood/Mud (Photo: Ritesh Shukla / Getty Images/CBS)

(CBS)–Kathmandu, Nepal — Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a hydropower tunnel Friday as emergency teams continued an operation to reach others believed to be trapped inside, officials said.

The two men were rescued from the Trishuli 3A tunnel nine days after floods, likely caused by a glacier collapse, devastated towns and swept away villages in Nepal on Aug. 26.

Nepalese lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane posted about the second rescue on his Facebook page shortly after army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet confirmed the first trapped worker’s rescue.

CBS News’ Ramy Inocencio reports that “there’s renewed hope that we might be seeing more survivors come out — possibly dozens more — because rescuers have already heard more voices deeper in those tunnels.”

A man who survived is carried on Sept. 4, 2026 by members of a search and rescue team. Nepal Army/Handout via REUTERS

Nepal Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told Inocencio in a text message that he’s “thrilled” about the two rescues and is “hoping to see more survivors.” He said it’s unclear how many survivors there are, but with those voices being heard, there are more people alive waiting to be saved and the clock is ticking to get to them.

Rescuers first heard voices from inside the tunnel Friday morning, confirming that people were alive and enabling them to locate the two men, Neupane said.

Local television news channels showed images of the first rescued worker covered in mud and being carried from the site on a rescuer’s shoulder. Officials said both men were in stable condition and were flown to a hospital in Kathmandu.

When mechanical foreman Sanjay Shah was pulled out, he said “thank you,” but he’s been advised not to talk anymore because of his condition, CBS News’ Inocencio says.

Amir Maharjan, brother of the other rescued worker, mechanical supervisor Kabir Maharjan, told The Associated Press he “can’t explain what we are feeling at the moment. We are just grateful to God.” He said the family was on its way to the hospital to see him.

Kabir Maharjan’s wife, Hirashova, told CBS News partner network BBC News, “We couldn’t properly eat or drink for 10 days. We were very scared. Now we are all happy. We are even crying.”

At least 557 workers are missing from the Trishuli 3A hydropower project along the Trishuli River, with about 115 believed to be trapped in the main tunnel, according to the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal.

Rescuers carry a survivor from a tunnel linked to a hydropower station at a location given as Rasuwa district, Nepal, in this image released on Sept. 4, 2026. Nepal Army/Handout via REUTERS

A Nepali energy adviser told Inocencio it’s not just a tunnel that goes into the ground next to the Trishuli River but a system of rooms and chambers that snake up and down, and that’s where the workers are apparently stuck.

The adviser also told Inocencio that the trapped workers are some of the smartest engineers in Nepal and they probably have been trying to figure their own way out and how to get oxygen so they don’t run out of air — the biggest risk.

At least 1,287 people were killed in the floods and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to the country’s disaster management agency. China, as of late Wednesday, said 21 people were killed and 541 were missing on the Tibet side of the border.

title: 2 people rescued alive from tunnel after deadly Nepal-Tibet flash flood - ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
description: 2 people rescued alive from tunnel after deadly Nepal-Tibet flash flood  ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
publisher.title: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
full_article:
LONDON -- Two people have been rescued from a hydropower tunnel at the Trishuli 3A construction site, Nepal's Army confirmed Friday after posting videos and images from the scene on Facebook.

Nepalese lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane, an engineer who has been involved in the search operations, also posted about the two rescues on his Facebook page, including photos and videos from the scene.

He identified the two workers rescued as Sanjay Sah and Kabir Maharjan.

In an earlier Facebook post, Neupane said rescuers had heard voices from people trapped inside the tunnel.

"It has been confirmed that more than one person's voice has been heard from inside," Neupane wrote in the post. "When the rescue team said, 'Don't panic, we are rescuing,' a response of 'yes' was received from inside."

After being rescued, Sah, a mechanical foreman, said in a video published by the Nepali Army on Friday that his responsibility was to save the lives of the others in the tunnel because he was in the control room.

"I told everyone that there was a big accident on the big dam, and asked everyone to run and in the end, I ran out of time and could not run out," Sah said in the video, which was translated from Nepali.

At least 557 workers are missing from the Trishuli 3A hydropower projects along the Trishuli River, with about 115 believed to be trapped in the tunnel, according to the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal.

Nepal's Communication Minister Bikram Timilsina said officials remain hopeful that more workers will be rescued. "We are waiting for the rescue of more and more people," Timilsina wrote on his Facebook page.

Soldiers rescue a worker alive from a tunnel during an ongoing operation at the Trishuli-3A hydropower project in Nepal's Rasuwa district, Sept. 4, 2026. Nepal Army

Sah said there seemed to be three or four more people still stuck in the tunnel, and possibly even more, as the tunnel is long and some may have been swept deeper inside.

Holding onto hope, Sah said he was chanting mantras while he was trapped.

The death toll following last week's unprecedented flash flood at the Nepal-Tibet border has climbed to 1,287, with an additional 4,216 people believed to still be missing as of Thursday, officials said.

Those figures increased from 1,114 deaths and 3,916 missing people, respectively, a day earlier, according to Nepal's National Disaster Management Authority.

Soldiers rescue a worker alive from a tunnel during an ongoing operation at the Trishuli-3A hydropower project in Nepal's Rasuwa district, Sept. 4, 2026. Nepal Army

Chinese state media have reported an additional 16 deaths and 546 missing people in Tibet, bringing the total death toll to 1,268 and the number of missing people on both sides of the border to 4,762.

Relief and rescue efforts are continuing, with almost all communication towers restored and nearly 12,000 people rescued through international and domestic aid.

Additionally, almost 21,500 security personnel have been mobilized in an effort to speed up search and rescue operations, with more than 5,000 people receiving treatment for injuries, officials said.

Nepali Prime Minister Shah said earlier this week that his government would begin focusing on "rehabilitation" as the length of time since the initial disaster grows.

title: Rapid response by AP dominates breaking news play of Nepal flash floods - ap.org
description: Rapid response by AP dominates breaking news play of Nepal flash floods  ap.org

full_article:
The AP team responding to devastating flash floods at the Nepal-China border overcame dangerous and serious logistical difficulties to dominate global coverage of what would become one of the biggest disasters in the Himalayan nation, wiping out entire villages and killing more than 1,000. Strong all-format coverage of the disaster caused by a glacial collapse showcased AP’s global teamwork and collaboration.

As soon as news broke about a massive flash flood hurtling down from the Himalayan mountains, Kathmandu photographer Niranjan Shrestha and video journalist Upendra Mansingh headed to Nuwakot, one of the worst-affected districts. Niranjan’s powerful first images, showing stunned survivors caked in mud, and Upendra’s compelling video brought to life the unprecedented scale of the unfolding disaster. Upendra provided an unmatched mobile live shot, showing the devastation hours ahead of the competition. The UGC team sprung into action, obtaining video of the terrifying moments when the flash flood hit an immigration center at the border crossing.

The Asia team quickly put into place a border-spanning, rapid-response text filing system to support the fast-moving story. Reporter Aijaz Hussain in New Delhi, India, along with local stringer Srishti Kafle, provided a stream of quick updates, while climate writer Sibi Arasu pitched in with reporting and explainers on the glacial collapse from Bengaluru.

In the days to come, more crews were deployed, and strong global teamwork produced an incredible package of personal narratives, explainers, dispatches, graphics, satellite imagery and maps, along with quick all-format updates.

The impressive cross-format reporting was reflected in the metrics, with extensive usage by global audiences and customers.

Judges praised the bravery and resourcefulness of the team in covering the immediate aftermath of the disaster. Their work dominated global coverage of the floods, demonstrated excellent collaboration and led to an engaging package of varied, cross-format work.

For rapid response and unmatched coverage of a top global story, Shrestha, Mansingh, Arasu, Hussain and Kafle win this week’s Best of the AP — First Winner.

नेपाल-चीन सीमा पर विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ि के जवाब दैत एपी टीम खतरनाक आ गंभीर रसद के कठिनाई के दूर क हिमालयी राष्ट्र के सबस पैघ आपदा मे स एक बनय वाला के वैश्विक कवरेज पर हावी भ गेल, जाहि मे पूरा गाम के सफाया भ गेल आ एक हजार स बेसी लोक के मौत भ जायत। हिमनदी केरऽ पतन के कारण पैदा होय वाला आपदा केरऽ मजबूत ऑल-फॉर्मेट कवरेज न॑ एपी केरऽ वैश्विक टीम वर्क आरू सहयोग के प्रदर्शन करलकै ।

हिमालय केरऽ पहाड़ स॑ नीचें दौड़तें-दौड़तें भारी फ्लैश फ्लड के खबर खुलतें ही काठमांडू केरऽ फोटोग्राफर निरंजन श्रेष्ठ आरू वीडियो पत्रकार उपेन्द्र मानसिंह सबस॑ बेसी प्रभावित जिला म॑ स॑ एक नुवाकोट के तरफ बढ़लै । निरंजन केरऽ शक्तिशाली पहिलऽ छवि, जेकरा म॑ स्तब्ध बची गेलऽ लोगऽ क॑ कीचड़ म॑ केक करी क॑ देखैलऽ गेलऽ छै, आरू उपेंद्र केरऽ सम्मोहक वीडियो न॑ खुलै वाला आपदा केरऽ अभूतपूर्व पैमाना क॑ जीवंत करी देलकै । उपेन्द्र न॑ एक बेजोड़ मोबाइल लाइव शॉट उपलब्ध कराय देलकै, जेकरा म॑ प्रतियोगिता स॑ घंटों आगू के तबाही के प्रदर्शन करलऽ गेलै । यूजीसी के टीम एक्शन में उछली पड़ल, ओहि भयावह क्षण के वीडियो प्राप्त केलक जखन सीमा क्रासिंग पर एकटा आप्रवासन केंद्र पर फ्लैश फ्लड आबि गेल छल.

एशिया टीम न॑ जल्दी स॑ तेजी स॑ चलै वाला कहानी क॑ समर्थन दै लेली सीमा प॑ फैललऽ, रैपिड-रिस्पांस टेक्स्ट फाइलिंग सिस्टम क॑ लागू करी देलकै । भारत केरऽ नई दिल्ली म॑ रिपोर्टर ऐजाज हुसैन न॑ स्थानीय स्ट्रिंगर सृष्टि काफ्ले के साथ त्वरित अपडेट के धारा उपलब्ध कराय देलकै, जबकि जलवायु लेखिका सिबी अरसू न॑ बेंगलुरु स॑ हिमनदी गिरै के रिपोर्टिंग आरू व्याख्याकारऽ के साथ अपनऽ बात रखलकै ।

आबै वाला दिनऽ म॑ आरू चालक दल केरऽ तैनाती करलऽ गेलै, आरू मजबूत वैश्विक टीमवर्क न॑ व्यक्तिगत कथ्य, व्याख्याकार, प्रेषण, ग्राफिक्स, उपग्रह छवि आरू नक्शा के एक अविश्वसनीय पैकेज के साथ-साथ त्वरित ऑल-फॉर्मेट अपडेट के निर्माण करलकै ।

प्रभावशाली क्रॉस-फॉर्मेट रिपोर्टिंग मेट्रिक्स म॑ परिलक्षित होय गेलै, जेकरऽ व्यापक उपयोग वैश्विक दर्शक आरू ग्राहकऽ न॑ करलकै ।

निर्णायक सब आपदा के तुरंत बाद के घटना के कवर करै में टीम के बहादुरी आरू साधन संपन्नता के प्रशंसा करलकै। हुनकऽ काम बाढ़ केरऽ वैश्विक कवरेज प॑ हावी रहलै, उत्कृष्ट सहयोग के प्रदर्शन करलकै आरू विविध, क्रॉस-फॉर्मेट काम केरऽ एगो आकर्षक पैकेज के तरफ ले गेलै ।

title: Rescuers pull 2 trapped workers from a hydropower tunnel 9 days after Nepal floods - latimes.com
description: Rescuers pull 2 trapped workers from a hydropower tunnel 9 days after Nepal floods  latimes.com
publisher.title: latimes.com
full_article:
KATHMANDU, Nepal — Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from an underground tunnel at a hydropower plant Friday, raising hopes of reaching dozens of others believed to be trapped nine days after deadly floods swept away villages and submerged the Himalayan region in mud and debris.

Search teams first heard voices from inside the tunnel in the morning, allowing them to locate the two men, Nepalese lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane said. Images showed a rescuer carrying one of the workers, covered in mud, on his back, while soldiers on either side helped.

One of those rescued said more people are alive inside the tunnel, according to army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, and the search is ongoing.

Advertisement

“I can’t explain what we are feeling at the moment. We are just grateful to god,” Amir Maharjan, the brother of one of those rescued, told The Associated Press.

Basnet confirmed the first trapped worker’s rescue, and Neupane posted about the second on his Facebook page shortly after.

Both men were flown to a hospital in Kathmandu, and Maharjan said his family was on its way there. One of the survivors was in critical condition, according to a statement from the prime minister’s office.

Advertisement

Officials identified the men as a mechanical foreman and a mechanical supervisor. They were rescued from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A plant.

About 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects in Nepal, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped in various tunnels, according to authorities.

About 115 are believed trapped in the tunnel at Trishuli 3A alone, according to the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal.

Nepal’s Communication Minister Bikram Timilsina wrote on his Facebook page that officials “are waiting for the rescue of more and more people.”

At least 1,287 people were killed in the Aug. 26 floods, likely caused by a glacier collapse, and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to Nepal’s disaster management agency. China said Friday 31 people were killed and 531 were missing on the Tibet side of the border, according to Chinese official news agency Xinhua.

Nepal’s disaster agency estimated Friday that flooding caused at least $2.5 billion in damage to infrastructure and property.

Advertisement

Kafle and Saaliq write for the Associated Press. Saaliq reported from New Delhi. AP journalist Kanis Leung in Hong Kong contributed to this report.

title: Nepal's catastrophic flash flood: The anatomy of surge water - South Carolina Public Radio
description: Nepal's catastrophic flash flood: The anatomy of surge water  South Carolina Public Radio
publisher.title: South Carolina Public Radio
full_article:
In minutes, rushing water can transform a swollen river into a destructive wall. In Nepal,

experts say flash flooding has shown just how quickly a catastrophic collapse can trigger the most violent flash flood in modern history.

This wasn’t the standard slow-rising flood, because at the altitude of 17,000 feet in the Himalayas, a section of a glacier snapped completely off a cliff face. As a result, between 100 million and 200 million cubic meters of ice rock dropped vertically down the mountain.

The friction of the falling ice and rock generated extreme heat, resulting in the ice melting quickly. The ice rock created a block in a narrow gorge and from intense pressure the gorge burst and released the devastating “water bomb” down the Bhote Koshi River Valley.

The 20 billion liters of fluid released could fill 8,000 Olympic-sized pools.

The Himalayan valleys are tight, steep, and V-shaped causing the energy of the surge to be tightly compressed and with nowhere to expand outward the liquid concrete wall of debris forced its way straight up.

Satellite data indicates that debris reached heights of 130 to 300 feet as it squeezed through the gorge. The water height itself peaked at 300 feet — nearly as tall as the Capital Center building in downtown Columbia, which is 349 feet.

The sheer force of the water — moving at 105 mph — meant that multi-story concrete structures stood no chance as it elevated high above the normal riverbed. As a result of this catastrophic flood, Nepal and Tibet has faced significant loss, with more than 1,000 confirmed fatalities and more than 4,400 people still missing, including tourist. More than 7,000 homes have been swept away, 19 critical bridges destroyed, and entire mountain villages buried under the thick soil.

For Nepal and Tibet, this was more than a flood. It was a loss of homes, livelihoods and loved ones, in minutes.

To stay updated for more information visit us online at South Carolina ETV and Public Radio.

title: Nepal’s Floods Upset Its China-India Balancing Act - The Diplomat – Asia-Pacific
description: Nepal’s Floods Upset Its China-India Balancing Act  The Diplomat – Asia-Pacific
publisher.title: The Diplomat – Asia-Pacific
full_article:
Nepal’s recent floods, which have killed at least 1,280 people while over 5,600 are still missing as of this writing, rank among the country’s worst natural disasters. Preliminary estimates put economic losses at $2.56 billion. But the disaster’s consequences will extend far beyond the immediate human and economic toll.

It has also undermined the efforts of successive post-2015 governments to achieve more geopolitical balance, largely through the development of new transport, trade and transit facilities with China.

As a landlocked country wedged between India and China, Nepal has long sought to preserve its strategic autonomy by balancing the influence of its two neighbors.

For a variety of reasons, India, which surrounds the country on three sides, has blockaded its open border with Nepal three times since 1969 — most recently in 2015. That year, Nepal promulgated a new constitution that had failed to address India’s concerns. At other times, New Delhi has openly meddled in Nepali politics.

To reduce that vulnerability to Indian pressure, Nepali rulers have felt the need to increase engagement with China, the northern neighbor.

After the 2015 blockade, the then-K.P. Sharma Oli government signed a slew of agreements with China to establish new trade and transit links. As part of the process, a significant investment was made to upgrade the Kerung border point (known as Gyirong on the Chinese side) into an all-weather international crossing. Much of China-Nepal trade has gradually shifted to Kerung from Tatopani, the previous main artery of bilateral trade that was badly damaged by the 2015 earthquakes.

Unfortunately, the recent floods literally washed away much of the investment around Kerung. There is not even a trace of the customs buildings and customs yards — on either side of the border.

After the flooding of the Kerung border, China has also shut down Tatopani, citing possible landslides on the Nepali side. (Beijing has also long been wary of the possible use of the Tatopani route by “Free Tibet” activists.) All cross-border traffic has been diverted to Korala, the third international border crossing between Nepal and China. But Korala is not an easy crossing, nor is there much in terms of cross-border trade infrastructure. Besides these three, the three other designated points for Nepal-China trade are minuscule and limited to handling local trade.

In the big picture, Nepal’s trade with China, which was already limited, will be further restricted after the floods.

India is Nepal’s largest trade partner, with China coming in at a distant second. The floods will exacerbate an already troubling imbalance. But Kathmandu’s options are limited. Rebuilding Kerung or upgrading Korala to handle more traffic will require a lot of time and money. Shipping goods from China is an option, but a costly one. The country’s dependence on India will thus further increase. Besides the prospect of some Indian goods replacing Chinese ones in Nepali markets, Nepal will now have to use Indian ports to import even vital supplies from China.

With the floods knocking out around 10 percent of Nepal’s electricity-generation capacity, the energy dependence on India could go up too.

The Rasuwa floods will strengthen the argument that geography leaves Nepal with no realistic substitute for India as its principal commercial and transit partner, with China serving mainly as a supplementary option. And as India’s commercial clout increases in Nepal, so will its strategic sway. Nepal, after all, shares a long, flat open border with India and the two countries are bound together by cultural and family ties.

Nepali Prime Minister Balen Shah had already complicated Nepal’s external relations with his unconventional approach, initially avoiding individual meetings with foreign envoys and senior visiting officials. Beijing, with whom Nepal will now have to work closely to rebuild damaged infrastructure along the border, was particularly displeased at what it saw as the Nepal government’s repeated failures to uphold the “One China” policy.

Yet rebuilding Nepal’s northern connectivity could itself have geopolitical consequences. Kathmandu will need Chinese technical and financial assistance to restore damaged border infrastructure. China will also be averse to involving other countries in reconstruction in the sensitive region. The floods could therefore produce a peculiar form of dual dependence: greater reliance on India for immediate trade and transit, even as Nepal turns to China to rebuild the infrastructure needed to reduce that very reliance.

For the 36-year-old Nepali prime minister, this creates a separate political dilemma. Shah will have to rely more on India for trade and connectivity while also being under pressure to maintain a safe distance from New Delhi — in keeping with the wishes of core nationalist constituencies.

The mountainous trade routes to China have long been vulnerable to landslides and earthquakes, limiting the northern neighbor’s viability as a trade and transit alternative to India. The recent disaster has highlighted this weakness like never before.

The floods will not change Nepal’s need to balance India and China. What they will change is the feasibility of one crucial component of that strategy.

केरुंग सीमा में बाढ़ि के बाद चीन नेपाली पक्ष के संभावित भूस्खलन के हवाला दैत ततोपानी सेहो बंद क देलक अछि। (बीजिंग सेहो बहुत दिन स “फ्री तिब्बत” कार्यकर्ता द्वारा ताटोपानी मार्ग के संभावित उपयोग स सावधान रहल अछि।) सीमा पार स सबटा यातायात कए नेपाल आ चीन क बीच तेसर अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सीमा क्रासिंग कोरला दिस मोड़ि देल गेल अछि। लेकिन कोराला कोनो आसान पार नै छै, नै ही सीमा पार स॑ व्यापारिक बुनियादी ढाँचा के मामला म॑ बहुत कुछ छै । एहि तीनू के अलावा नेपाल-चीन व्यापार के लेल तीन अन्य निर्धारित बिन्दु माइनस अछि आ स्थानीय व्यापार के संभालबा तक सीमित अछि।

बड़का तस्वीर मे चीन के संग नेपाल के व्यापार जे पहिने सं सीमित छल, बाढ़ि के बाद आओर रोकल जाएत.

भारत नेपाल केरऽ सबसें बड़ऽ व्यापारिक भागीदार छै, जेकरा म॑ चीन दूर केरऽ सेकेंड प॑ आबी रहलऽ छै । बाढ़ि पहिने सं परेशान करय वाला असंतुलन के आओर बढ़ा देत. मुदा काठमांडू’क विकल्प सीमित अछि. केरुंग के पुनर्निर्माण या कोराला के अपग्रेड करय लेल बेसी ट्रैफिक के संभालय लेल बहुत समय आओर पैसा के जरूरत पड़त. चीन सं सामान भेजब एकटा विकल्प अछि, मुदा महग. एहि तरहें देशक भारत पर निर्भरता आओर बढ़त. नेपाली बाजार मे चीनी माल के जगह किछु भारतीय सामान के संभावना के अलावा आब नेपाल के चीन सं महत्वपूर्ण आपूर्ति तक आयात करय लेल भारतीय बंदरगाह के उपयोग करय पड़त.

बाढ़ि के कारण नेपाल के बिजली उत्पादन क्षमता के करीब 10 प्रतिशत हिस्सा के खटखटाबय के कारण भारत पर ऊर्जा के निर्भरता सेहो बढ़ि सकैत अछि.

रसुवा बाढ़ि ई तर्क क॑ मजबूत करतै कि भूगोल न॑ नेपाल क॑ भारत केरऽ प्रमुख वाणिज्यिक आरू पारगमन भागीदार के रूप म॑ कोय यथार्थवादी विकल्प नै छोड़ी देल॑ छै, जेकरा म॑ चीन मुख्य रूप स॑ पूरक विकल्प के रूप म॑ काम करै छै । आरू जेना-जेना भारत केरऽ व्यापारिक दबदबा नेपाल म॑ बढ़तै, ओकरऽ रणनीतिक दबदबा भी बढ़तै । नेपाल आखिर भारतक संग एकटा लंबा, समतल खुला सीमा साझा करैत अछि आ दुनू देश सांस्कृतिक आ पारिवारिक संबंध सँ एक दोसरा सँ बान्हल अछि ।

नेपाली प्रधानमन्त्री बलेन शाह अपन अपरंपरागत दृष्टिकोणसँ नेपालक विदेश सम्बन्धकेँ जटिल बना देने छल, शुरूमे विदेशी दूत आ वरिष्ठ आगंतुक अधिकारीसभसँ व्यक्तिगत बैसारसँ बचैत छल । बीजिंग, जिनका साथ नेपाल क॑ अब॑ सीमा के किनारे क्षतिग्रस्त बुनियादी ढाँचा के पुनर्निर्माण लेली बारीकी स॑ काम करना पड़ी जैतै, ओकरा ई बात स॑ खास तौर प॑ नाराजगी छेलै कि ओकरा नेपाल सरकार केरऽ बार-बार “एक चीन” नीति क॑ कायम रखै म॑ विफलता देखलऽ गेलै ।

तइयो नेपाल के उत्तरी संपर्क के पुनर्निर्माण के स्वयं भूराजनीतिक परिणाम भ सकैत अछि. काठमांडू क्षतिग्रस्त सीमा बुनियादी ढांचा के बहाल करय लेल चीन के तकनीकी आ आर्थिक सहयोग के जरूरत पड़त. चीन संवेदनशील क्षेत्र मँ पुनर्निर्माण मँ दोसरौ देशौ क शामिल करै स॑ भी परहेज करतै । अतः बाढ़ि स॑ दोहरी निर्भरता केरऽ एगो विचित्र रूप पैदा होय सकै छै : तत्काल व्यापार आरू पारगमन लेली भारत प॑ अधिक निर्भरता, यहाँ तलक कि नेपाल वू ही निर्भरता क॑ कम करै लेली जरूरी बुनियादी ढाँचा के पुनर्निर्माण लेली चीन के तरफ मुड़ै छै ।

३६ वर्षीय नेपाली प्रधानमन्त्रीके लेल ई अलग राजनीतिक दुविधा उत्पन्न करैत अछि । शाह क॑ व्यापार आरू कनेक्टिविटी लेली भारत प॑ अधिक भरोसा करना पड़ी जैतै आरू साथ ही साथ नई दिल्ली स॑ सुरक्षित दूरी बनाबै के दबाव भी छै — कोर राष्ट्रवादी क्षेत्रऽ के इच्छा के अनुरूप ।

चीन जाय वाला पहाड़ी व्यापारिक मार्ग बहुत दिन स॑ भूस्खलन आरू भूकंप के शिकार रहलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ भारत केरऽ व्यापार आरू पारगमन विकल्प के रूप म॑ उत्तरी पड़ोसी देश केरऽ व्यवहार्यता सीमित होय गेलऽ छै । हाल के आपदा एहि कमजोरी के ओहिना उजागर केलक अछि जेना पहिने कहियो नहि छल.

बाढ़ि सं नेपाल के भारत आ चीन के संतुलन बनेबाक जरूरत मे कोनो बदलाव नहिं आओत. ओ सब जे बदलताह ओ अछि ओहि रणनीति क एकटा महत्वपूर्ण घटक क व्यवहार्यता।

Death toll rises Nepal focuses on reconstruction The threat of El Niño

The miraculous rescue of two Nepalese men who had spent nine days trapped in a tunnel at a hydroelectric power station since the fateful flash flood on 26 August has made headlines in the international media as a small ray of hope amidst the tragedy.

The efforts of the rescue teams who have been working over the past week at the Trishuli 3A hydroelectric power station to find the people trapped in the tunnels alive have paid off: Sanjay Sha, aged 30, and Kabir Maharjan, aged 45, were rescued early this morning, 4 September, and taken to a hospital in the Nepalese capital, Kathmandu.

Sanjay Sah, a survivor rescued from a tunnel at the Upper Trishuli 3A hydroelectric project nine days after the deadly floods and a landslide, is being transferred for air evacuation to Kathmandu from a military base in Nuwakot, Nepal, on 4 September 2026 – REUTERS/ ATHIT PERAWONGMETHA

Rescue teams are confident of finding more survivors in the same tunnel, through which workers at the hydroelectric power station tried to escape moments after the flash flood struck on 26 August.

Death toll rises

The good news of this rescue is merely a drop in the ocean of despair. The latest update on the number of victims and missing persons from the Nepalese Government’s National Disaster Management Authority, published at midday on Thursday 3 September, showed the figures had risen.

The official death toll across Nepal and the Tibet region now stands at 1,252 (up from the 1,114) reported just 24 hours earlier), whilst a total of 4,216 people remain missing.

googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('zone_184558'); });

Members of the Nepalese Army carry a survivor, Kabir Maharjan, who was rescued from a tunnel at the Upper Trishuli 3A hydroelectric power station, nine days after the deadly flash floods and a landslide, after being flown by helicopter from a military base in Nuwakot to Kathmandu, Nepal, on 4 September 2026 – REUTERS/ DIPEN SHESTHA

For its part, China has not updated its casualty figures since last Wednesday, 2 September, and maintains the figure of 21 dead and more than 500 missing.

In any case, rescue operations are proving extremely difficult, as teams are being forced to dig by hand because it is impossible to use machinery that could trigger further landslides.

Hira Sobha Maharjan, wife of Kabir Maharjan – a survivor who was rescued from a tunnel at the Upper Trishuli 3A hydroelectric project nine days after the deadly floods and a landslide – speaks to the press at a military hospital in Kathmandu, Nepal, on 4 September 2026 – REUTERS/RANUP SHRESTHA

The Nepalese authorities have reported that there are still more than 900 workers, a large proportion of whom are foreign nationals, missing from the various energy projects in the Himalayan region affected by the flash floods.

On a positive note, the number of people rescued thanks to national and international cooperation stands at over 12,000. Of these, 5,000 are receiving treatment for their injuries in various hospitals and health centres.

Rescue team members are working hard to gain access to the tunnel at the Upper Trishuli 3A hydroelectric power station whilst searching for survivors and recovering bodies in Rasuwa, Nepal, on 3 September 2026 - REUTERS/NAVESH CHITRAKAR

More than 21,500 security personnel are involved in the search and rescue operations, supported by various teams from several countries, who are working round the clock to try to find the missing people alive.

The body of a victim, recovered from the Upper Trishuli 3B hydroelectric power station, is being taken to a military base following the deadly flash floods and landslides that struck Nuwakot (Nepal) on 4 September 2026 - REUTERS/NAVESH CHITRAKAR

Nepal focuses on reconstruction

The Nepalese Prime Minister, Balendra Shah, has stated that as time passes since the disaster struck, his government will focus on the reconstruction of the affected areas.

Shah has held talks with various international leaders, including Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, whom he thanked for his solidarity and assistance with the rescue efforts, which include the deployment of a team of Australian drone specialists to help locate those missing.

Members of the Nepal Army’s search and rescue team are working near a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydroelectric project following the devastating floods and landslides that struck the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa, Nepal, on 4 September 2026 – Nepal Army/Image provided via REUTERS

The Nepalese Prime Minister maintains that the flash floods and flooding, caused by a glacier collapse, are an unfortunate consequence of climate change.

The threat of El Niño

Just a few hours ago, the World Meteorological Organisation warned that the phenomenon known as El Niño will reach very strong intensity over the coming months and will increase the risk of extreme weather events well into 2027.

Rescue team members attempt to reach the rubble of a building near the entrance to the Upper Trishuli 3A hydroelectric power station tunnel following the deadly flash floods and landslide, whilst searching for survivors and recovering bodies in Rasuwa, Nepal, on 3 September 2026 - REUTERS/ NAVESH CHITRAKAR

According to the organisation’s statement, the probability of El Niño persisting until February 2027 is exceptionally high, at almost 100 per cent. In the words of Celeste Saulo, Secretary-General of the World Meteorological Organisation, “despite its seemingly harmless name, El Niño has the potential to deal a severe blow to communities and economies around the world. We are witnessing the disruption and devastation caused by droughts and floods, and forecasts suggest these effects will worsen as El Niño intensifies”.

Heavy machinery is working to clear the path to the entrance of a tunnel at the Upper Trishuli 3A hydroelectric power station following deadly flash floods and landslides, whilst the search for survivors continues in Rasuwa, Nepal, on 3 September 2026 - REUTERS/NAVESH CHITRAKAR

For the head of the organisation, “this exceptional El Niño event calls for exceptional preparedness and response measures. In the WMO’s 50-year history, we have never before undertaken such a major mobilisation alongside the National Meteorological and Hydrological Services (NMHSs), which lead the provision of forecasts and services to save lives and protect livelihoods”.

खोज आरू बचाव अभियान म॑ २१,५०० स॑ भी अधिक सुरक्षाकर्मी शामिल छै, जेकरा म॑ कई देशऽ के विभिन्न टीमऽ के सहयोग छै, जे लापता लोगऽ क॑ जिंदा खोजै के कोशिश म॑ चौबीसों घंटा काम करी रहलऽ छै ।

4 सितम्बर 2026 क नुवाकोट (नेपाल) मे आयल घातक आकस्मिक बाढ़ आ भूस्खलन के बाद अपर त्रिशुली 3 बी जलविद्युत स्टेशन स बरामद एकटा पीड़ित के शव के सैन्य अड्डा ल जा रहल अछि - रायटर/नवेश चित्रकार

नेपाल पुनर्निर्माण पर केन्द्रित अछि

नेपालके प्रधानमन्त्री बलेन्द्र शाह आपदा आएल समय बीतैत गेलाक बाद हुनकर सरकार प्रभावित क्षेत्रके पुनर्निर्माणमेकेन्द्रित होएत बतौलनि अछि ।

शाह न॑ ऑस्ट्रेलिया केरऽ प्रधानमंत्री एंथोनी अल्बानीस सहित विभिन्न अंतर्राष्ट्रीय नेता सिनी स॑ बातचीत करल॑ छै, जेकरा हुनी बचाव प्रयासऽ म॑ एकजुटता आरू सहायता लेली धन्यवाद देलकै, जेकरा म॑ लापता लोगऽ के पता लगाबै म॑ मदद करै लेली ऑस्ट्रेलियाई ड्रोन विशेषज्ञऽ के टीम के तैनाती भी शामिल छै ।

नेपाल केरऽ रसुवा म॑ ४ सितम्बर २०२६ क॑ भोटेकोशी नदी प॑ पड़लऽ विनाशकारी बाढ़ आरू भूस्खलन के बाद त्रिशुली ३ए जलविद्युत परियोजना केरऽ सुरंग के पास नेपाल सेना केरऽ खोज आरू बचाव टीम के सदस्य काम करी रहलऽ छै – नेपाल सेना/Image provided via REUTERS

नेपाल के प्रधानमंत्री के कहना छै कि ग्लेशियर के गिरला के कारण आकस्मिक बाढ़ आरू बाढ़ जलवायु परिवर्तन के दुर्भाग्यपूर्ण परिणाम छै ।

संगठन केरऽ बयान के अनुसार फरवरी २०२७ तलक एल नीनो केरऽ कायम रहै के संभावना असाधारण रूप स॑ अधिक छै, जे लगभग १०० प्रतिशत छै । विश्व मौसम संगठन केरऽ महासचिव सेलेस्टे साउलो के शब्दऽ म॑ कहलऽ जाय त॑ “अपनऽ हानिरहित प्रतीत होय वाला नाम के बावजूद एल नीनो म॑ दुनिया भर के समुदाय आरू अर्थव्यवस्था प॑ भारी झटका लगै के क्षमता छै ।हम॑ सूखा आरू बाढ़ के वजह स॑ पैदा होय वाला व्यवधान आरू तबाही के गवाह बनी रहलऽ छियै आरू पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार एल नीनो के तेज होय के साथ ई प्रभाव आरू खराब होय जैतै” ।

घातक आकस्मिक बाढ़ आ भूस्खलन के बाद अपर त्रिशुली 3ए जलविद्युत स्टेशन पर सुरंग के प्रवेश द्वार के रास्ता साफ करय लेल भारी मशीनरी काज क रहल अछि, जखन कि नेपाल के रसुवा में 3 सितंबर 2026 के बचि गेल लोक के खोज जारी अछि - रायटर/नवेश चित्रकार

संगठन केरऽ प्रमुख लेली, “ई असाधारण एल नीनो आयोजन म॑ असाधारण तत्परता आरू प्रतिक्रिया के उपाय के जरूरत छै ।डब्ल्यूएमओ केरऽ ५० साल के इतिहास म॑ हम्मं॑ पहल॑ कहियो राष्ट्रीय मौसम आरू जल विज्ञान सेवा (एनएमएचएस) के साथ-साथ एतना बड़ऽ जुटान नै करलकै, जे जीवन बचाबै आरू आजीविका के सुरक्षा लेली पूर्वानुमान आरू सेवा के प्रावधान के नेतृत्व करै छै” ।

KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a hydropower tunnel Friday as emergency teams continued an operation to reach others believed to be trapped inside, officials said.

The two men were rescued from the Trishuli 3A tunnel nine days after floods, likely caused by a glacier collapse, devastated towns and swept away villages in Nepal on Aug. 26.

Nepalese lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane posted about the second rescue on his Facebook page shortly after army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet confirmed the first trapped worker’s rescue. Officials identified the two men as a mechanical foreman and a mechanical supervisor.

Nepal’s Communication Minister Bikram Timilsina said officials remain hopeful that more workers will be rescued.

“We are waiting for the rescue of more and more people,” Timilsina wrote on his Facebook page.

full_article:
Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a hydropower tunnel Friday, raising hopes of reaching a dozen others believed to be trapped nine days after catastrophic floods devastated towns and swept away villages.

The two men were rescued from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A construction site. The rescued workers were Sanjay Sah, a mechanical foreman, and Kabir Maharjan, a mechanical supervisor, Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha’s office said in a statement.

When the mountain gave way above the Nepali power plant ‌where Sah worked, he said he chose to stay and help instead of fleeing.

"I was in the control room in the tunnel. Normally there are four to six ​people there, but there could have been 40 to 45 people that ⁠day," the 30-year-old told ⁠army officials from a stretcher, an oxygen mask ‌strapped to his face, in a video shared by the Nepalese authorities.

"My responsibility was to save everyone's lives. When there was such a big accident, it was not right for me to run away."

Sah said he had warned the others the ⁠moment word came of the disaster upstream, urging them to flee. He never made it out himself. By the time he turned to run, there was no time left.

Nepalese lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane posted about the second rescue on his Facebook page shortly after army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet confirmed the first trapped worker's rescue.

Members of the Nepal Army move a rescued tunnel survivor after he was airlifted from an army base in Nuwakot to Kathmandu. (Dipen Shrestha/Reuters)

Basnet said one of the survivors told rescuers that more people were still alive inside the tunnel.

Rescuers first heard voices from inside the tunnel Friday morning, confirming that people were alive and allowing them to locate the two men, Neupane said.

Hopes of finding survivors dim a week after catastrophic Nepal flood

Local television news channels showed images of the first rescued worker covered in mud and being carried from the site on a rescuer's shoulder. One of the survivors was in a critical condition, according to a statement from the Nepal prime minister's office. Both men were flown to a hospital in Kathmandu.

"I can't explain what we are feeling at the moment. We are just grateful to god," Amir Maharjan, brother to one of the rescued workers, told The Associated Press. He said the family was on its way to the hospital to see him.

Hundreds of other workers still missing

At least 557 workers are missing from the Trishuli 3A hydropower project along the Trishuli River, with about 115 believed to be trapped in the tunnel, according to the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal.

Nepal's Communication Minister Bikram Timilsina said officials remain hopeful that more workers will be rescued.

Hundreds feared stuck in hydropower tunnels as flood deaths surpass 950 in Nepal, China

"We are waiting for the rescue of more and more people," Timilsina wrote on his Facebook page.

At least 1,259 people were killed in the Aug. 26 floods, likely caused by a glacier collapse, and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to the country's disaster management agency.

China said Friday 31 people were killed and 531 were missing on the Tibet side of the border, according to Chinese official news agency Xinhua.

About 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects in Nepal, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped in tunnels, according to local authorities.

"हमर जिम्मेदारी छल जे सबहक जान बचाबी। जखन एतेक पैघ दुर्घटना भेल छल तखन हमरा लेल भागब ठीक नहि छल।"

फोटो | नेपालमे फंसल मजदूरके उद्धार : १.

साह कहलकै कि हुनी दोसरऽ लोगऽ क॑ चेतावनी देल॑ छेलै कि ⁠क्षण ऊपर केरऽ आपदा के खबर आबी गेलै, जेकरा म॑ ओकरा सिनी क॑ भागै के आग्रह करलऽ गेलै । ओ कहियो स्वयं एकरा नहि बनौलनि। जाबे ओ दौड़य लेल घुमल ताबे समय नहि रहि गेल छल।

नेपाली विधायक श्री राम न्यौपाने सेना प्रवक्ता ब्रिगेडियर एस. जेनरल राजा राम बस्नेट पहिल फंसल मजदूर के बचाव के पुष्टि केलनि।

नुवाकोट के सेना अड्डा स काठमांडू हवाई जहाज स लऽ गेलाक बाद बचावल गेल सुरंग स बचि गेल व्यक्ति के नेपाली सेना के सदस्य सब स्थानांतरित करैत अछि । (दीपेन श्रेष्ठ/रायटर)

बस्नेट कहलनि जे, बचि गेल लोक मे सं एकटा बचावकर्मी के कहलक जे सुरंग के अंदर एखनो आओर लोक जीवित अछि.

न्यूपाने कहलनि जे, बचावकर्मी सब सं पहिने शुक्रदिन भोर मे सुरंग के अंदर सं आवाज सुनलक, जाहि सं लोक जीवित हेबाक पुष्टि भेल आ दुनू गोटे के पता लगेबाक अनुमति भेटल।

नेपाल केरऽ विनाशकारी बाढ़ के एक सप्ताह बाद बचे वाला मिलै के आशा मंद होय गेलै

स्थानीय टेलीविजन न्यूज चैनल सब में पहिल बचावकर्मी के तस्वीर देखाओल गेल जे कीचड़ में ढंकल छल आ एकटा बचावकर्मी के कान्ह पर जगह सं ल जा रहल छल. नेपाल प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालयके विज्ञप्तिमे बचि गेल एक गोटेके अवस्था गम्भीर रहल । दुनू गोटे के विमान सं काठमांडू के अस्पताल पहुंचाओल गेल.

बचावल गेल एकटा मजदूर के भाई अमीर महर्जन द एसोसिएटेड प्रेस के कहलनि जे, हम ई नहि बता सकैत छी जे एखन हमरा सब के की महसूस भ रहल अछि, हम सब सिर्फ भगवान के आभारी छी। ओ कहलनि जे, परिवार हुनका देखय लेल अस्पताल जा रहल छल।

सैकड़ों आओर मजदूर एखनो लापता अछि

त्रिशूली नदीक कात मे बनल त्रिशूली ३ ए जलविद्युत परियोजना सँ कम सँ कम ५५७ मजदूर लापता अछि, जाहि मे लगभग ११५ गोटे सुरंग मे फँसल मानल जा रहल अछि, नेपालक स्वतन्त्र विद्युत उत्पादक संघ जनौलक अछि ।

नेपालके संचार मन्त्री बिक्रम तिमिलसिना आरो मजदुरके उद्धार होबयके अधिकारीसब आशा बनल रहल बतौलनि ।

चीन के नेपाल मे बाढ़ि सं मृतक के संख्या 950 सं बेसि भ गेलाक कारण सैकड़ों लोक जलविद्युत सुरंग मे फंसला के आशंका अछि

तिमिलसिना अपन फेसबुक पेज पर लिखलनि जे, हम सब बेसी स बेसी लोक के बचाव के इंतजार क रहल छी।

देश केरऽ आपदा प्रबंधन एजेंसी के अनुसार 26 अगस्त क॑ ऐलऽ बाढ़ म॑ कम स॑ कम १,२५९ लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलऽ छै, जेकरऽ कारण संभवतः ग्लेशियर केरऽ गिरला के कारण होय गेलऽ छै आरू ५,००० स॑ भी अधिक लोग लापता छै ।

चीन केरऽ आधिकारिक समाचार एजेंसी सिन्हुआ के अनुसार चीन न॑ शुक्रवार क॑ कहलकै कि सीमा केरऽ तिब्बत तरफ ३१ लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलै आरू ५३१ लोग लापता छै ।

नेपालके १२ जलविद्युत परियोजनासँ करिब ९०० मजदूर लापता अछि, जाहिमे मोटा-मोटी ५०० मजदुर सुरंगमे फँसल आशंका रहल स्थानीय प्राधिकारी जनौलक अछि ।

Search teams first heard voices from inside the tunnel in the morning, allowing them to locate the two men, Nepalese lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane said. Images showed a rescuer carrying one of the workers, covered in mud, on his back, while soldiers on either side helped.

One of those rescued said more people are alive inside the tunnel, according to army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, and the search is ongoing.

“I can’t explain what we are feeling at the moment. We are just grateful to god,” Amir Maharjan, the brother of one of those rescued, told The Associated Press.

Basnet confirmed the first trapped worker’s rescue, and Neupane posted about the second on his Facebook page shortly after.

Video below: Comparative satellite image of Nepal-China border

Both men were flown to a hospital in Kathmandu, and Maharjan said his family was on its way there. One of the survivors was in critical condition, according to a statement from the prime minister’s office.

Officials identified the men as a mechanical foreman and a mechanical supervisor. They were rescued from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A plant.

About 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects in Nepal, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped in tunnels, according to authorities.

About 115 are believed trapped in the tunnel at Trishuli 3A alone, according to the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal.

Nepal’s Communication Minister Bikram Timilsina wrote on his Facebook page that officials “are waiting for the rescue of more and more people.”

At least 1,287 people were killed in the Aug. 26 floods, likely caused by a glacier collapse, and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to the country’s disaster management agency. China said late Wednesday that 21 people were killed and 541 were missing on the Tibet side of the border.

Nepal’s disaster agency estimated Friday that flooding caused at least 387.5 billion Nepalese rupees ($2.5 billion) in damage to infrastructure and property.

publisher.title: New Security Beat
full_article:
This piece was adapted from an earlier Stimson Center Commentary, “ A Cascading Disaster on the China–Nepal Border: What to Know About the August 2026 Rasuwa Flood, 72 Hours Later , ” and updated to reflect current conditions.



On August 26, 2026, a massive volume of bedrock and glacial ice broke loose 5,200 meters above sea level on the north side of Nepal’s Langtang range, triggering a “rock-ice avalanche” that crashed into the Lhende River on the Nepal-China border fueling the deadliest extreme flow disaster on record in the country. This cascade barreled downstream at an average of ~160 kilometers per hour downstream toward the Nepal-China border. It slammed into and overwhelmed Chinese border facilities at Rasuwagadhi just 7.5 minutes after the mountain gave way, then tore across the border and down the Bhotekoshi/Trishuli River corridor into Nepal, swallowing towns and causing extensive damage over 100 kilometers from its source.

As of 2:00pm ET on September 3rd a total of 1,259 people are confirmed dead and over 5,000 people are still reported missing. These numbers include Nepalis living and working along the river corridor, hundreds of foreign tourists visiting the Langtang region and pilgrims crossing to Mount Kailash, and hundreds of hydropower workers trapped in tunnels. The border town of Timure and the market hub of Syaphrubesi were essentially wiped away; 19 bridges and 40 kilometers of highway are gone, and more than 430 megawatts of hydropower capacity, representing more than 10% of Nepal’s national supply, is offline

Cropped from Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi Flood: Search, Rescue and Relief Response, Situation Response #3 , Issued September 3, 2026. Source: National Disaster Risk Reduction & Management Authority (NDRRMA), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of Nepal

The residents of Nepal’s Rasuwa district, which includes a large Tamang population, have lived with disaster risk (e.g. floods, landslides, earthquakes, and avalanches) for centuries and they have adapted to and managed these risks. But the risks are changing fast, and the level of exposure communities face today is unprecedented.

I say this, having spent nearly 14 years conducting research in this river basin (in all of the affected settlements in Rasuwa), having led post-disaster relief activities in many of these towns after the 2015 Gorkha earthquake, and having personally survived a massive glacier avalanche on the other side of the very same mountain, which led to years of research and direct engagement. None of this is abstract to me, and my heart breaks for Rasuwa again.

A Cascade, Not a Rainfall Disaster

This catastrophic event happened on a clear day. Unlike many of Nepal’s recent disasters, it wasn’t triggered by extreme rainfall or an earthquake, and surprisingly, given the volume of water, there wasn’t a lake involved. Post-event analysis points to an unexpected culprit: the sheer force of the rock-ice avalanche that became more flood-like as it gathered water, rock, and sediment and funneled through the Trishuli’s tight canyons, arriving downstream as a fast-moving wall of concrete. This was a single, continuous, cascading extreme flow event.

Figure 1: Map of the impacted areas with timestamps for flood propagation (Source: CLaSH, Accessed September 2, 2026)

Scientists are still working to establish whether climate change played a role in destabilizing the source area, and formal processes of evaluating attribution are now underway. But the frequency of extreme flow events in recent years suggests that climate change is destabilizing the mountain cryosphere across the Himalayan region. Simply put, warming and climatic volatility can impact glaciers, weaken permafrost, and drive rapid or unseasonal changes in snowpack. In Nepal, climate-related risks interact with monsoon dynamics and seismic risk to compound danger in ways that existing monitoring frameworks aren’t built to see.

This event joins a grim and growing list of Himalayan cascading disasters — the 2021 Chamoli flood, the 2021 Melamchi disaster, the 2023 South Lhonak GLOF (Glacial Lake Outburst Flow), and the 2025 Blatten collapse in Switzerland. Notably, a smaller glacial flood struck this exact watershed in July 2025, destroying the same border bridge and killing 19 people — a warning sign that didn’t translate into readiness for what came next.

Of Blind Spots and Needles in Haystacks

It would be wrong to read this as a failure of Nepal’s early warning systems. The source area sits in a genuine gap — a narrow sliver of unpopulated Nepali territory that drains north into China, falling between the scientific attention long focused on the south side of the Langtang range and the Chinese monitoring effort that intensified after last year’s flood. Nepal’s gauge and station networks were built to catch monsoon floods and glacial lake outbursts, not a catastrophic flow that outran any possible alert. But generating alerts for an event like this isn’t just a problem of data scarcity or blind spots, it’s also a problem of speed and scale. The Himalaya has more slopes capable of failing this catastrophically, across more vertical relief, than anywhere else on Earth. Scientists can and have highlighted a variety of high-risk areas and landforms, but finding subtle changes in a timely fashion requires skillfully separating signal from noise as risk changes across the Himalaya.

The overall point is that experts need a signal to effectively direct their tools and attention – and finding these signals can often feel like finding needles in Himalaya haystacks. Of roughly a dozen extreme flow events in the region over the past decade, only one — the 2023 South Lhonak outburst — struck a site already flagged as risky. Every other event originated from somewhere no one was watching, including this one.

Learning from Disasters Like This

Each event offers lessons and insights that allow us to return with greater precision and a new understanding of where similar hazard chains might be stacking up. For example, the 2024 Thame (GLOF) taught researchers that small glacial lakes can grow dangerously fast; last year’s transboundary flood event along the same Lhende River into Rasuwa showed that supraglacial lakes — lakes on top of glaciers — can expand and drain catastrophically. Last week’s event highlights the increasing prevalence of another kind of risk: showing how an ice-rock avalanche can trigger a massive flood-like event and impact communities more than 100 kilometers downstream.

Tools are rapidly developing, but no single instrument will catch everything, so the approach has to be layered — weather stations and river gauges as a foundation, satellite monitoring to track remote terrain, seismic networks to triangulate a failure within seconds, and, critically, local observers such as herders, mountaineers, and fishers who can flag a crack or a filling lake long before a sensor does. Even a few minutes of warning can be the difference between an evacuation and a recovery operation.

What the Stimson Nepal Early Warning Team is Doing

In the wake of this event, on the Stimson Center’s Early Warning for Cascading Disasters in Nepal project team, working in Nepal and Washington, rapidly mobilized to assess the event, gather information, and share expert analysis with Government of Nepal institutions such as the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) and government hydrologists and meteorologists. Using Sentinel-1, Landsat, and Planet Labs imagery, we identified the avalanche’s source, ruled out a supraglacial lake we had assessed last year, and confirmed the landslide-dam mechanism. We also tasked commercial radar/SAR imagery from ICEYE US over the source and blockage sites and delivered pre- and post-event comparisons to NDRRMA and Nepal’s Home Ministry within hours.

After two new lakes formed in the avalanche flowpath — one along the Lhende River, another high in the upper catchment — we worked with the NDRRMA to assess changing conditions, analyze breach scenarios, and provide scientific analysis of the flood pulses that came when the lake began to finally drain on August 30th. Members of our team also contributed to the HIRISK rapid assessment, prepared by an international group of Chinese, Nepali, American, Austrian, Swiss, and Dutch scientists, which was published on August 28.

Lingering Risks and Uncertainties, in Both Nepal and China

Risks remain throughout the region, and heavy rain could still reactivate destabilized slopes or remobilize other landforms within the impacted area. Critically, the monsoon season is not yet over. There are risks that we know of, such as risks from specific glacial lakes in China. But we can’t discount the risks we are not yet aware of from other potential cascading hazards. Monitoring these risks often requires both focused efforts on high-risk areas and triaging between uncertainties.

In this wake of this devastating event, we are already seeing better transboundary coordination between Nepal and China. High-priority information is being shared and new channels of communication opened between Chinese and Nepali authorities — a promising, if overdue, shift. A variety of people have called for greater formal coordination and the establishment of transboundary monitoring networks.

To be clear, no one — not Nepal, not China, not the international scientific community — could have identified the subtle changes and specific risks that triggered this disaster. Forensic analysis is yielding new insights that we can use to search for similar risks in the future, but this event began with a sudden mass movement that turned into an extreme flow far too fast for a true alert to be shared. The hope is that this disaster will catalyze the kind of sustained, cross-border monitoring and cooperation the region has needed for years.

नेपाल केरऽ रसुवा जिला केरऽ निवासी, जेकरा म॑ तामांग केरऽ एगो बड़ऽ आबादी शामिल छै, सदियो स॑ आपदा केरऽ जोखिम (जैना बाढ़, भूस्खलन, भूकंप, आरू हिमस्खलन) के साथ जी रहलऽ छै आरू वू ई जोखिमऽ के अनुकूल होय गेलऽ छै आरू ओकरऽ प्रबंधन करी चुकलऽ छै । लेकिन जोखिम तेजी स॑ बदली रहलऽ छै, आरू आज समुदायऽ क॑ जेतना एक्सपोजर के सामना करना पड़ै छै, वू अभूतपूर्व छै ।

हम ई बात कहैत छी, लगभग 14 साल एहि नदी बेसिन में (रसुवा के सब प्रभावित बस्ती में) शोध करय में बितेलहुं, 2015 के गोरखा भूकंप के बाद एहि में सं बहुतो शहर में आपदा के बाद राहत गतिविधि के नेतृत्व केने छी, आ व्यक्तिगत रूप सं ठीक ओही पहाड़ के दोसर कात एकटा विशाल ग्लेशियर हिमस्खलन सं बचलहुं, जाहि सं सालों सं शोध आ प्रत्यक्ष संलग्नता भेल. एहि मे सँ कोनो बात हमरा लेल अमूर्त नहि अछि, आ हमर मोन फेर रसुवा लेल टूटि जाइत अछि।

एकटा झरना, बरखाक आपदा नहि

ई विनाशकारी घटना साफ दिन मे घटित भेल। नेपाल केरऽ हाल केरऽ बहुत आपदा के विपरीत ई अत्यधिक वर्षा या भूकंप स॑ नै शुरू होय गेलऽ छेलै, आरू आश्चर्य के बात छै कि पानी केरऽ मात्रा क॑ देखत॑ हुअ॑ एकरा म॑ कोनो झील नै छेलै । घटना के बाद के विश्लेषण एकटा अप्रत्याशित अपराधी दिस इशारा करैत अछि : चट्टान-बर्फ के हिमस्खलन के सरासर बल जे पानि, चट्टान आ तलछट के जमा करैत बाढ़ि सन बेसी भ गेल आ त्रिशुली के कड़ा घाटी में फनल करैत, कंक्रीटक तेजी सं चलैत देबाल के रूप में नीचा पहुंचैत. ई एकटा एकल, निरंतर, झरना-झरना चरम प्रवाहक घटना छल ।

चित्र 1: बाढ़ प्रसार कें लेल समय मुहर कें साथ प्रभावित क्षेत्रक कें नक्शा (स्रोत: CLaSH, अभिगमन तिथि 2 सितंबर, 2026)

वैज्ञानिक सब अखनी भी ई स्थापित करै के काम करी रहलऽ छै कि जलवायु परिवर्तन न॑ स्रोत क्षेत्र क॑ अस्थिर करै म॑ भूमिका निभैलकै कि नै, आरू अब॑ एट्रिब्यूशन के मूल्यांकन के औपचारिक प्रक्रिया चलैलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै । लेकिन हाल के सालऽ म॑ चरम प्रवाह के घटना के आवृत्ति स॑ ई बात के संकेत मिलै छै कि जलवायु परिवर्तन पूरा हिमालयी क्षेत्र म॑ पहाड़ी क्रायोस्फीयर क॑ अस्थिर करी रहलऽ छै । सीधा शब्दऽ म॑ कहलऽ जाय त॑ गर्मी आरू जलवायु अस्थिरता ग्लेशियर प॑ प्रभाव डाल॑ सकै छै, परमाफ्रॉस्ट क॑ कमजोर करी सकै छै आरू स्नोपैक म॑ तेजी स॑ या गैर-मौसम परिवर्तन क॑ बढ़ावा द॑ सकै छै । नेपाल मे जलवायु सं जुड़ल जोखिम मानसून गतिशीलता आ भूकंपीय जोखिम कें साथ बातचीत करयत छै आ खतरा कें बढ़ाबै छै जे मौजूदा निगरानी ढाँचा देखय कें लेल नहि बनायल गेल छै.

ई घटना हिमालय केरऽ झरना वाला आपदा केरऽ एगो भयावह आरू बढ़तऽ सूची म॑ शामिल होय जाय छै — २०२१ केरऽ चमोली बाढ़, २०२१ केरऽ मेलमची आपदा, २०२३ केरऽ साउथ ल्होनक जीएलओएफ (ग्लेशियल लेक आउटबर्स्ट फ्लो), आरू २०२५ म॑ स्विट्जरलैंड म॑ ब्लैटन केरऽ पतन । उल्लेखनीय छै कि जुलाई 2025 म॑ ई सटीक जल-विभाजन म॑ एगो छोटऽ हिमनदी बाढ़ आबी गेलै, जेकरा म॑ वही सीमा पुल क॑ नष्ट करी देलऽ गेलै आरू 19 लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलै — एगो चेतावनी संकेत जेकरऽ अनुवाद आगू की होतै ओकरा लेली तत्परता म॑ नै बदललै ।

घास के ढेर में अंधा धब्बे एवं सुई के

एकरा नेपाल केरऽ पूर्व चेतावनी प्रणाली केरऽ विफलता के रूप म॑ पढ़ना गलत होतै । स्रोत क्षेत्र एगो वास्तविक अंतराल म॑ बैठलऽ छै — अजनबी नेपाली इलाका केरऽ एगो संकीर्ण टुकड़ा जे उत्तर तरफ चीन म॑ बह॑ छै, जे लंबा समय स॑ लैंगटांग श्रृंखला केरऽ दक्षिणी तरफ केंद्रित वैज्ञानिक ध्यान आरू चीनी निगरानी प्रयास के बीच गिरै छै जे पिछला साल केरऽ बाढ़ के बाद तेज होय गेलऽ छै । नेपाल केरऽ गेज आरू स्टेशन नेटवर्क मानसून केरऽ बाढ़ आरू हिमनदी झील केरऽ विस्फोट क॑ पकड़ै लेली बनलऽ छेलै, नै कि कोनो भी संभावित अलर्ट स॑ आगू बढ़ै वाला विनाशकारी प्रवाह । मुदा एहि तरहक इवेंट के लेल अलर्ट जेनरेट करब सिर्फ डाटा के कमी या ब्लाइंड स्पॉट के समस्या नहिं अछि, ई स्पीड आओर स्केल के सेहो समस्या अछि. हिमालय केरऽ ढलान पृथ्वी केरऽ अन्य जगहऽ स॑ भी अधिक ढलान छै जे एकरा विनाशकारी रूप स॑ विफल करै म॑ सक्षम छै, अधिक ऊर्ध्वाधर राहत के पार । वैज्ञानिकऽ न॑ विभिन्न प्रकार के उच्च जोखिम वाला क्षेत्र आरू भू-रूप क॑ उजागर करी सकै छै आरू करी चुकलऽ छै, लेकिन समय प॑ सूक्ष्म परिवर्तन खोजै लेली हिमालय भर म॑ जोखिम म॑ बदलाव के साथ-साथ संकेत क॑ शोर स॑ कुशलता स॑ अलग करै के जरूरत छै ।

समग्र बात ई छै कि विशेषज्ञऽ क॑ अपनऽ औजार आरू ध्यान क॑ प्रभावी ढंग स॑ निर्देशित करै लेली एगो संकेत के जरूरत छै – आरू ई संकेतऽ क॑ खोजना अक्सर हिमालय केरऽ घास के ढेर म॑ सुई खोजै के तरह महसूस होय सकै छै । पिछला एक दशक मँ ई क्षेत्र मँ लगभग एक दर्जन चरम प्रवाह घटना मँ सँ केवल एक - २०२३ केरौ दक्षिण ल्होनाक विस्फोट - एगो ऐसनौ जगह प हमला करलकै जेकरा पहिने सँ जोखिम भरलौ के रूप मँ चिन्हित करलौ गेलौ छेलै । आन सभ आयोजन कतहु सँ उत्पन्न भेल छल जतय कियो नहि देखैत छल, जाहि मे ई आयोजन सेहो शामिल छल ।

एहि तरहक आपदा स सीखब

प्रत्येक आयोजन सबक आ अंतर्दृष्टि प्रदान करयत छै जे हमरा बेसि परिशुद्धता आ एकटा नव समझ कें साथ वापस आवय कें अनुमति देयत छै की समान खतरा श्रृंखला कतय ढेर भ सकय छै. जेना, 2024 केरऽ टेम (GLOF) न॑ शोधकर्ता सिनी क॑ सिखाबै छेलै कि छोटऽ-छोटऽ हिमनदी झील खतरनाक रूप स॑ तेजी स॑ बढ़ी सकै छै ; पिछला साल वही ल्हेंडे नदी के किनारे रसुवा में सीमा पार के बाढ़ के घटना स॑ पता चललै कि सुप्रैग्लेशियल झील — ग्लेशियर के ऊपर झील — विस्तार करी सकै छै आरू विनाशकारी रूप स॑ पानी निकासी करी सकै छै । पिछला सप्ताह केरऽ ई आयोजन एगो आरू तरह के जोखिम के बढ़तऽ प्रसार प॑ प्रकाश डालै छै: ई देखाबै छै कि कोना बर्फ-चट्टानऽ के हिमस्खलन एगो बड़ऽ बाढ़ जैसनऽ घटना क॑ शुरू करी सकै छै आरू 100 किलोमीटर स॑ भी अधिक नीचें के समुदायऽ प॑ प्रभाव डाल॑ सकै छै ।

उपकरण तेजी स॑ विकसित होय रहलऽ छै, लेकिन कोय भी एक उपकरण सब कुछ नै पकड़तै, ई लेली ई दृष्टिकोण क॑ परतदार बनाबै ल॑ पड़तै — मौसम स्टेशन आरू नदी गेज क॑ नींव के रूप म॑, दूरस्थ इलाका क॑ ट्रैक करै लेली उपग्रह निगरानी, ​​सेकंड के भीतर विफलता क॑ त्रिकोणीय करै लेली भूकंपीय नेटवर्क, आरू, महत्वपूर्ण रूप स॑, स्थानीय पर्यवेक्षक जेना कि चरवाहा, पर्वतारोही, आरू मछुआरा जे कोनो सेंसर स॑ बहुत पहलें दरार या भरना झील क॑ झंडा देखा सकै छै । किच्छू मिनटक कें चेतावनी कें सेहो निकासी आ रिकवरी ऑपरेशन कें बीच अंतर भ सकएय छै.

स्टिमसन नेपाल पूर्व चेतावनी दल की क रहल अछि

ई आयोजन के मद्देनजर नेपाल आरू वाशिंगटन म॑ काम करै वाला स्टिमसन सेंटर केरऽ नेपाल म॑ झरना वाला आपदा लेली प्रारंभिक चेतावनी परियोजना टीम प॑ तेजी स॑ आयोजन के आकलन करै, जानकारी जुटाबै, आरू नेपाल सरकार केरऽ संस्थान जेना कि राष्ट्रीय आपदा जोखिम कम करै आरू प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण (एनडीआरआरएएमए) आरू सरकारी जलविज्ञानी आरू मौसम वैज्ञानिकऽ के साथ विशेषज्ञ विश्लेषण साझा करै लेली जुटलऽ छेलै । सेंटिनल-1, लैंडसैट, आरू प्लैनेट लैब केरऽ इमेजरी के उपयोग करी क॑ हम्मं॑ हिमस्खलन केरऽ स्रोत के पहचान करलियै, पिछला साल हम्मं॑ आकलन करलऽ गेलऽ सुप्रैग्लेशियल झील क॑ खारिज करी देल॑ छेलियै आरू भूस्खलन-डैम तंत्र के पुष्टि करल॑ छेलियै । हम स्रोत आरू रुकावट स्थल के ऊपर आईसीईई यूएस स॑ वाणिज्यिक रडार/एसएआर इमेजरी क॑ भी काम सौंपलकै आरू घंटऽ के भीतर एनडीआरआरएएमए आरू नेपाल केरऽ गृह मंत्रालय क॑ घटना स॑ पहल॑ आरू बाद के तुलना पहुँचैलकै ।

हिमस्खलन प्रवाहमार्ग में दू टा नव झील बनलाक बाद - एकटा ल्हेन्डे नदीक कात, दोसर ऊपरी जलग्रहण क्षेत्र में ऊँच - हम एनडीआरआरएएमए के संग मिलिकय बदलैत परिस्थिति के आकलन केलहुं, उल्लंघन के परिदृश्य के विश्लेषण केलहुं, आ बाढ़ के दाल के वैज्ञानिक विश्लेषण उपलब्ध करौलहुं जे 30 अगस्त के अंततः झील में पानी निकलय लागल. हमरऽ टीम के सदस्यऽ न॑ चीनी, नेपाली, अमेरिकी, ऑस्ट्रियाई, स्विस, आरू डच वैज्ञानिकऽ के एगो अंतर्राष्ट्रीय समूह द्वारा तैयार करलऽ गेलऽ HIRISK रैपिड आकलन म॑ भी योगदान देलकै, जे २८ अगस्त क॑ प्रकाशित करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

विलम्बित जोखिम आ अनिश्चितता, नेपाल आ चीन दुनू मे

पूरा क्षेत्र म॑ जोखिम बनलऽ छै, आरू भारी बारिश स॑ अखनी भी अस्थिर ढलान क॑ पुनः सक्रिय करलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै या प्रभावित क्षेत्र के भीतर अन्य भू-रूप क॑ पुनः गतिशील करलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै । आलोचनात्मक रूप स मानसून क मौसम एखन खत्म नहि भेल अछि। जोखिम छै जे हमरा सब क॑ पता छै, जेना कि चीन केरऽ विशिष्ट हिमनदी झीलऽ स॑ जोखिम । मुदा हम ओहि जोखिम कें छूट नहि द’ सकैत छी जकर जानकारी हमरा सभ कें एखन धरि नहिं अछि, अन्य संभावित झरना खतरा सं. अइ जोखिम कें निगरानी कें लेल अक्सर उच्च जोखिम वाला क्षेत्रक पर केंद्रित प्रयास आ अनिश्चितताक कें बीच परीक्षण दूनू कें आवश्यकता होयत छै.

एहि विनाशकारी घटनाक एहि मद्देनजर नेपाल आ चीनक बीच सीमा पारक बेहतर समन्वय हमरा लोकनि पहिने सँ देखि रहल छी । उच्च प्राथमिकता वाला जानकारी साझा करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै आरू चीनी आरू नेपाली अधिकारियऽ के बीच संचार केरऽ नया चैनल खुल॑ लगलऽ छै — ई आशाजनक, अगर समय सीमा स॑ भी होय गेलऽ छै त॑ बदलाव । कई तरह के लोगऽ न॑ अधिक औपचारिक समन्वय आरू सीमा पार निगरानी नेटवर्क के स्थापना के आह्वान करल॑ छै ।

स्पष्ट कहै लेली कि कोय भी — नेपाल नै, चीन नै, अंतर्राष्ट्रीय वैज्ञानिक समुदाय नै — ई आपदा के शुरुआत करै वाला सूक्ष्म परिवर्तन आरू विशिष्ट जोखिम के पहचान नै करी सकै छेलै । फोरेंसिक विश्लेषण स॑ नया-नया अंतर्दृष्टि मिल॑ लगलऽ छै जेकरऽ उपयोग हम्मं॑ भविष्य म॑ भी ऐसनऽ जोखिम के खोज करै लेली करी सकै छियै, लेकिन ई घटना के शुरुआत अचानक एगो जन आंदोलन स॑ होलै जे बहुत तेजी स॑ चरम प्रवाह म॑ बदली गेलै जेकरा स॑ एक सच्चा अलर्ट साझा नै करलऽ जाब॑ सक॑ । आशा छै कि ई आपदा वू तरह के निरंतर, सीमा पार स॑ निगरानी आरू सहयोग के उत्प्रेरक बनतै जेकरऽ जरूरत ई क्षेत्र क॑ सालौ स॑ छै ।
